Lemma
[the poles theorem reduces to the rays being pullback-geodesics]

↗ lem:dc-ch7-3-4-pole-diffeo ↗ lem:dc-ch7-3-4-pullback-metric

1. ch7:3.4Let $M$ be a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold, $p\in M$, and $f:T_pM\to M$ a smooth local diffeomorphism which is metric-expanding for its own pulled-back metric $f^*g$. If for every $v\in T_pM$ the radial line $\gamma _v(s)=s\, v$ is a geodesic of $f^*g$, then $f$ is a diffeomorphism $T_pM\to M$.
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch7-3-4-pole-diffeo \sketch In the identity chart on $T_pM$, $\gamma _v(s)=sv$ has zero second derivative. Thus the geodesic condition is exactly $\Gamma ^{f^*g}_{sv}(v,v)=0$; the remaining initial-data conditions are immediate, so the pole lemma applies.

□
